note: D1's window on the gate's real delivery (the third Phase 1 review, chapter 15.4 B-48): trace-gate01-rist-20010 with its AAC PID 200 (lead p50 0.17 s) stamped 3.9 s later, about lead_max_ns + 70 ms. Under lines that the gate's +-300 ms delivery keeps a few ms to some 100 ms above their floor, PID 200 reads past 4 s: jitter, not a backlog (the floor gap is under backlog_ns), so it is never stale and nothing says backlog. It is the lead row's: timing from the video PID 100, whose clock locks at 308 s since B-100 (the first fit on the full window's densest band; 178 s before it, by the luck of the first bucket) and relocks on the envelope step at 325 s; degraded (lead) at 332 s, B-8's clamp on PID 200 at once, told every 30 s. Each switch is one timeline (B-96): the entries drop 120-200 ms per PID at once and the recovery leaves one gap per PID. Since B-90 the recovery clock restarts only where a row fails: the program recovers at 362 s, steps again at 375 s and fails again at 380 s, the clamp 1.4 s later, each switch moving PID 200 by its 4 s lead: 9.5 s dropped and 5.5 s of gaps in all, 7 gaps (before B-100: locked 178 s, the step 186 s, degraded 195 s, recovered 346 s, degraded 380 s; 9.6 s dropped: the flapping at another phase). The clamp locks are fresh ClockLocks and wait their own 300 s window on this scattered PID (7 clamp events, 10 before B-100). The rate: +21 ppm, no 'Source clock off' warning (before B-100 the relock epoch's chained fit took it to -121 ppm with the warning on 67 posts). Before B-48: 34.5 s of PID 200 dropped as overlap (backlog) in 733 events with gap markers, no clamp.
